rows.medi_said: Review. What was the word for review?
rows.amal_said: As a noun it's مراجعة. So what's-- what is it as a verb? ... صح، براجع.
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked for the word; sheet rows 'review | Muraaja3a | مراجعة' and 'i review | Ana baraaje3 | أنا براجع'.

rows.medi_said: آآآ، الشمال الـ، روسيا the, the north of Russia. الشمال.
rows.amal_said: بس، بس شمال روسيا.
rows.why: Idafa: the first word takes no el-; he put الـ on شمال, she recast شمال روسيا (again at 05:37) and he still said 'الشمال روس بيكون' at 06:02 which she let pass.

rows.medi_said: الشمال الـ، روس شمال؟ Did you say? رو... شس...
rows.amal_said: نويل، بس شمال روسيا.
rows.why: Truncated/wrong form of the country name (روس = Russians) three times 04:54, 05:33, 06:02; she supplied روسيا; may be a restart rather than a form error.

rows.medi_said: برد كتير ويكون بيمطر أو بتثلج.
rows.why: Plain-present ykoon without b- in an ordinary statement (no modal or time word before it); she only echoed مطر، ثلج.
rows.english: very cold and it rains or snows

rows.medi_said: آآآ ومغني نوع مغيمة.
rows.amal_said: تقدر تحط الدنيا قبل... like الدنيا مطر وثلج، و... مغيمة وعتمة.
rows.why: مغني (singer) is a different word from مغيمة (cloudy); sheet 'it's cloudy | M8ayyme | مغيمة'; she recast the weather list with مغيمة.

rows.medi_said: آآآ ومغني نوع مغيمة.
rows.why: English calque 'kind of cloudy' using نوع (sheet 'type / kind | Noa3 | نوع'), which does not mean 'somewhat'; she let it pass.

rows.medi_said: How do I say dark again؟
rows.amal_said: عتمة.
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked; sheet 'darkness | 3etme | عتمة'.

rows.medi_said: Is it Asafa؟ Is that, is that stars؟
rows.amal_said: No. ... Storm. ... One star is نجمة. What's multiple؟
rows.why: He offered عاصفة (sheet 'storm | 3aasefe | عاصفة') for 'stars'; she said No, Storm, then supplied نجمة/نجوم.

rows.medi_said: is it أنجم؟ I don't know. أنجم، نجوم،
rows.amal_said: نجوم.
rows.why: Invented plural pattern أنجم before landing on نجوم; she asked for the plural and confirmed نجوم.

rows.medi_said: الـ المدينة حوالين or الـ المدينة سان فرانسيسكو Oakland ... قريب، قريبًا ... مني.
rows.amal_said: What's the، what's-- وشو جمع غريب؟ ... غراب.
rows.why: Plural subject (the cities) needs the plural adjective قراب; he used singular قريب and the MSA adverb قريباً (her sheet: 'soon | qareeban'); she asked شو جمع قريب and he produced قراب.
rows.english: the cities around (SF, Oakland) are close to me

rows.medi_said: الـ المدينة حوالين or الـ المدينة سان فرانسيسكو Oakland
rows.why: Singular مدينة for 'the cities around' (he names two cities); she only fixed the adjective's plural, not the noun.

rows.medi_said: الـ المدينة حوالين or الـ المدينة سان فرانسيسكو Oakland
rows.why: English 'or' dropped inside an Arabic sentence; sheet 'or | Aw | أو'; he used أو correctly at 06:19.

rows.medi_said: نعيد ... بنعيد ... الـ.
rows.amal_said: بنقيم. ... قبل ما نزيد بيه، شو بنقيم؟
rows.why: He echoed her meta-verb بنقيم (we remove the -aan) as بنعيد; she repeated بنقيم and later spelled the steps; a hearing slip on a word she introduced, kept apart as listening.

rows.medi_said: تحت الكلمة.
rows.amal_said: The end. ... مم، آخر الكلمة. وبعدين؟
rows.why: تحت (under) for آخر (end); she prompted 'The end' until he said آخر الكلمة; sheet 'last / the end of | 2aa5er | آخر'.

rows.medi_said: آآآ، ع الـ-- أول الكلمة. ... الأول الـ-- فعل الكلمة.
rows.amal_said: لا، أول الكلمة.
rows.why: Idafa head takes no el-; she said لا، أول الكلمة; he repeated الأول at 12:50 and she let it pass (mm-hmm).

rows.medi_said: means to make something stop working.
rows.amal_said: مم. It's not بخرب yet. It's بخرب. (bkharreb vs bkhrab)
rows.wrong: بخرب = to make something stop working
rows.right: بخرَب = I stop working / break down (بخرِّب is the causative)
rows.why: He read the plain form as the make-X causative; she said it's not بخرّب yet, and he then said 'I stop working' (13:23).

rows.medi_said: آآآ، هي خربات.
rows.amal_said: mm-hmm. خربت.
rows.why: She-form past ending stretched to -aat; she recast خربت (again at 16:21 when he asked 'خربات or خربات'); may be vowel length (F2) rather than the ending itself.

rows.medi_said: with AC, can I say that? Air conditioning. تباي.
rows.amal_said: مم. تبعيت. We don't-- We haven't discussed تبعيت a lot yet. So تبعيت.
rows.why: Possessive particle تبع + ending for 'my AC'; he said تباي and she supplied the full form, but the transcript garbles her word.

rows.medi_said: صححته.
rows.amal_said: صلحته.
rows.why: صحّح (to correct) is a different verb from صلّح (to fix/repair); she recast صلحته and he repeated it; صلّح is not on her sheet; could also be a one-letter slip.

rows.medi_said: because [his Arabic sentence 19:11-20:06 untranscribed]
rows.amal_said: بس still هذا الفعل الثاني. ... أمم، not بخرب. بخرب that would be. ... you weren't trying to say she make it stop working.
rows.why: She said 'still the second verb', 'not بخرّب' and asked whether he meant 'she makes it stop working'; he confirmed he meant 'it stops working', so he had used the causative shape; his Arabic is untranscribed.

rows.medi_said: Um, [speaking Arabic]
rows.amal_said: So it's, it's, it's just إشي. Everything my girlfriend, my fiancée uses. So it's one thing.
rows.why: She stressed 'just إشي ... one thing': كل + singular = every/everything; his words are not transcribed.

rows.medi_said: Oh, but yeah, but [speaking Arabic] and then it's becha... ... oh, that's right, it's she and not you.
rows.amal_said: بتستعمل.
rows.why: He used the you-form for 'she uses' and admitted 'it's she and not you' (21:19); she recast بتستعمل twice (20:58, 21:13).

rows.medi_said: Uh, but [speaking Arabic] oh, that's right, it's she and not you. [speaking Arabic]
rows.amal_said: بتستعمله. ... كل إشي بتستعمله بيخرب.
rows.why: The object كل إشي is fronted, so the verb needs the -o pointer; she recast بتستعمله and then the full sentence at 21:53.

rows.medi_said: ما، ما تفتحي. ... ما بهتي، ما بهتي. بي-- بتفتحي
rows.amal_said: With B. ... ما بتحطي...
rows.why: فتح (open) for حط (put) in 'if you don't put it in the fridge'; sheet 'i put | Ana ba7ut | أنا بحط' and 'she put | heyye 7attat | هي حطت'; she recast ما بتحطي.
rows.english: if you don't put (it in the fridge)

rows.medi_said: ما، ما تفتحي.
rows.amal_said: With B. ... ما بتحطي...
rows.why: After إذا ما she wanted the b-verb (negative condition 'if you don't put'), not the negative-command shape ما ت-; she said 'With B'. Note bucket B3 says no b- after iza, but Amal kept the b- here in the negative.

rows.medi_said: إذا ما بتفتحي، ... هي الثلاجة.
rows.why: Repeated فتح (open) for حط (put) one minute after her fix at 25:08; she said ممتاز and moved on.
rows.english: if you don't put (it in the fridge)

rows.medi_said: هي الثلاجة.
rows.why: 'in the fridge' needs the preposition بـ and the verb needs the -ه object; he said هي الثلاجة (she/this fridge); she let it pass.

rows.medi_said: شوي يعني تذاكر.
rows.amal_said: tickets.
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked what تذاكر means; sheet 'ticket | Tazkara | تذكرة'.

rows.medi_said: [يضحك] لازم. اه، خرب
rows.amal_said: عزومة is feminine or masculine؟ ... خربت.
rows.why: العزومة is feminine so the past verb needs -t; she prompted with the gender question and then said خربت.

rows.medi_said: [speaking Arabic]
rows.amal_said: ما؟ ... ما it didn't come. ... ما أجا.
rows.why: She prompted ما ... and supplied ما أجا (it didn't come) for his sentence about the ruined dinner; his attempt is not transcribed.

rows.medi_said: So don't break it. I mean, you could use that as a command, right? ... Well, don't make it stop working, right? Not don't stop working.
rows.amal_said: Don't break something would be the other one. ... مم، no, it would be don't stop working.
rows.right: ما تخرب = don't stop working / don't get ruined (ما تخرّب = don't break it)
rows.why: Second time he read the plain form as the causative; she said no twice and named the other (doubled) verb as 'don't break something'.

rows.medi_said: Uh, ثانورك.
rows.amal_said: Mm-mm. تنورة is skirt.
rows.why: تنورة (sheet 'skirt | Tannoora | تنورة') for 'dress' (sheet 'dress | Fus6aan | فستان'); she said mm-mm, skirt; he then said فستانك and she confirmed.

rows.medi_said: هي, uh, خربت غرفةك.
rows.why: Feminine noun grows -t before the owner ending (her sheet writes 8urfet noam); the transcript's غرفةك suggests he dropped it; she said mm-hmm.

rows.medi_said: شو خرب? ... Uh, جلايك.
rows.amal_said: جلاية؟ So ... جلايتك.
rows.why: جلاية is feminine, so -t before -ك; she prompted with the bare noun and he produced جلايتك (40:26), which she confirmed.

rows.medi_said: مش قصدهم ... إنّه...
rows.amal_said: مش، مش أزتم or it's past also.
rows.why: 'They didn't mean to' is past and needs كان; he used the present pattern from her sheet ('i didn't mean it | Mish azdi | مش قصدي'); she said 'it's past also' and he reached ما كان قصدهم at 42:45.

rows.medi_said: Uh, مش كان and, uh, مش...
rows.amal_said: Not مش. [تضحك] If you use can. Not can. (= not مش if you use كان)
rows.why: The verb كان is negated with ما, not مش; she said 'Not مش', he fixed to ما كان قصدهم and she said ممتاز.

rows.medi_said: kharabu.
rows.amal_said: So، في عندنا خلاص ما can is a verb. Because can and then the verb after it should be what؟ (= ما كان قصدهم is a verb, the verb after it should be what?)
rows.why: After ما كان قصدهم the next verb is bare present (no b-, not past); he offered past خربوا, she asked what the verb after it should be, he gave yecharbu (43:10) and she said صح. He had also inserted إنّه at 42:26.
rows.english: they didn't mean to ruin your work

rows.medi_said: it would be echarrab, echarrbi. ... So echarrab, echarr, no? No, so charrab.
rows.amal_said: So it's بخرررب. There is a, there is a double medal here. ... No. ... خرب. ... When do I not put the a in command؟
rows.why: The command of a doubled-middle verb takes no initial vowel; she said No, خرّب, and quizzed him on when the a- is dropped.

rows.medi_said: Uh, shu, shu ahki? Shu tehki? Shu haket li? ... haket li. Shu haket li?
rows.amal_said: حكيت صح. ... حكيت لك صح.
rows.why: Asking Amal (f) 'what did you say to me' needs the inti past ending -ti; she answered the question ('I said صح') instead of correcting the form.
rows.english: what did you say to me?

rows.medi_said: uh, bidullu, bidullu, um, yikharabu. Keeps, uh, yikharabu?
rows.amal_said: Mm-mm, no. [speaks Arabic] ... So they are what's breaking.
rows.why: She said no to his 'bidullu yikharabu' for 'they keep breaking down'; her fix is untranscribed; the extra vowel in yikharabu points at the causative shape, and she then asked 'so they are what's breaking?'.
rows.english: why do your keys keep breaking down?

rows.medi_said: bitakhra- bitakhar- bitakhrobi. Bitakhrib.
rows.amal_said: Did you? ... [Medi 53:55: kharabtihum] ... Mm-hmm.
rows.why: 'Did you break them' is past; he used present بتخربي, she repeated 'Did you?', he said 'Oh, past tense' and gave خربتيهم.

rows.medi_said: sawarna kharab. Uh, ... were ruined. Kharabu. No. Kha-- uh, khar- kharabu. Kharabu.
rows.amal_said: Which, which one is it? [speaks Arabic]
rows.why: He wavered between خرب and خربوا for 'our photos were ruined'; she asked which one and supplied the form (untranscribed); a non-human plural normally takes the feminine singular verb.

rows.medi_said: rah yitkhar-- rah titkharabi. ... Yeah, rah titkharabi. Rah atkharabt. ... rah titkharabiha.
rows.amal_said: ليش؟ You would ruin it? ... No two T. Why two Ts؟ شوربة is feminine. So... ... one T. ... اه، راح تخربيها.
rows.why: tit-kharabi has an extra t (a gets-ruined shape, 'you would be ruined') where 'you'll ruin the soup' needs tkharrbi plus the -ha object pointing at feminine شوربة; she said 'No two T' and 'شوربة is feminine, so...' until he reached تخربيها.

rows.medi_said: rah yikhrab.
rows.amal_said: Yes, بس we're talking about شوربة. So... ... صح.
rows.why: شوربة is feminine so 'it will go bad' takes t-; she prompted with the gender and he fixed to tikhreb, which she confirmed صح.
